title: Willingness toward COVID-19 vaccination, coadministration with other vaccines and receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster: a cross-sectional study on the guardians of children in China.
ehr_evidence: The study used a self-administered questionnaire distributed through the 'Xiao Dou Miao' app. The study used online questionnaires and self-administered surveys.
summary: A cross-sectional study investigating the willingness of guardians in China to vaccinate children against COVID-19, coadminister vaccines, and receive booster doses.
key_findings: 86.68% of guardians were willing to vaccinate their children with the COVID-19 vaccine.
Guardians aged ≥40 years, healthcare workers, and those with children aged ≥3 years were more willing to vaccinate their children.
Approximately 77% of the guardians were willing toward the coadministration of COVID-19 and influenza vaccines.
86.68% of guardians were willing to vaccinate children with COVID-19 vaccine
77% were willing toward coadministration of influenza and COVID-19 vaccines
64% were willing toward coadministration of nonimmunization program vaccines
82% were willing to vaccinate children with a COVID-19 vaccine booster
population: Guardians of children aged <6 years in China
limitations: Potential selection bias from app users
Online questionnaire prevents effective random sampling
Not representative of the whole population in China
Self-administered questionnaires may have information deviation
